messages.subject: Stats Boot Camps and other training opportunities
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to advertise these highly recommended wildlife statistics training courses run by Mike Meredith and his colleagues in SE Asia. I know very few other people who can explain concepts in simpler words than Mike Meredith. Highly recommended courses.

Best regards  ---- Marc

Workshops: "Boot Camp" in Wildlife Study Design and Data Analysis

 = Mandalay, Myanmar, 2-14 July 2019.
 = Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, 8-19 July 2019 (just before ICCB).

The 10-day Boot Camp targets wildlife researchers familiar with field techniques but who have forgotten all the stats they were taught. We begin with simple concepts of binary and count data, but using a Bayesian framework. Bayes Rule is introduced on Day 2 and we see MCMC output on Day 3. We spend one day on MLE methods and AIC, and use both MLE and Bayesian analysis for occupancy, density and survival estimation in the last part of the workshop.

We believe that understanding of concepts comes from exploration of ideas with examples and activities, and we use practical activities and games throughout. Learning stats can be challenging, but it should be fun too.

Good results depend on a good design for data collection, and we spend about a third of the time on study design, both in general and specifically for occupancy, SCR and survival.

We use R a lot but assume no previous knowledge of R, just basic computer literacy: we begin with basics and provide one-on-one support when writing code. Lots of Bayes, but we don't use JAGS or show people how to write models in the BUGS language: that's another workshop.

More information at bcss.org.my.
